title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II
statement_short: Given a binary tree, populate each next pointer to point to its next right node. If there is no next right node, the next pointer should be set to NULL.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 6000, -100 <= Node.val <= 100
hint: Node count up to 6000 allows level-by-level traversal using next pointers of the previous level for O(1) space.
keywords: next pointer to point to its next right node
next pointer should be set to NULL
why_not: Right: Tree BFS traverses the tree level by level using a queue (or dummy head pointers for O(1) space) to connect adjacent right nodes in O(n) time. Not Tree DFS: DFS handles next pointers but requires careful order traversal and recursive stack memory. Not Linked List (Fast & Slow): Fast and slow pointers detect cycles rather than establishing cross-branch horizontal next pointers. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointer pairs across non-linear structures fails without level-order tracking.
